headline: Steady performance; healthy toll growth and O&M order book to drive earnings

highlights: Revenue included a) gain on InvITs & Related Assets as per fair value measurement, and b) dividend/interest income from InvITs & Related Assets.  EBITDA margins came in at 55.6% (v/s our estimate of 53%) in 2QFY27 (+280bp YoY and +165bp QoQ).

EBITDA grew ~14% YoY to INR10.5b (in line).  APAT grew 85% to INR2.6b (31% above estimate), led by low interest cost.  Construction revenue stood at INR8.2b (flat YoY); BOT revenue stood at INR7.2b (+15% YoY); and InvIT & related assets revenue stood at INR3.5b.  IRB declared an interim dividend of INR0.05 per equity share.  Order book stands at ~INR433b (excl.
GST) as at the end of Sep’26.  During 1HFY27, revenue/EBITDA/APAT grew by 5%/18%/65%.  IRB delivered a steady performance, supported by rising toll collections.
The company is strategically focusing on bidding for toll-operate-transfer (ToT) projects and building a sustainable O&M order book.
valuation: Revenue included a) gain on InvITs & Related Assets as per fair value measurement, and b) dividend/interest income from InvITs & Related Assets.  EBITDA margins came in at 55.6% (v/s our estimate of 53%) in 2QFY27 (+280bp YoY and +165bp QoQ).

However, management expects road project awarding to pick up in 2HFY27, as delays arising from NHAI's evaluation of compensation mechanisms for MLFF-based tolling have now been resolved.  Management indicated that 2QFY27 interest expense level should be considered the new quarterly run rate, with further reductions expected as the wholly owned SPVs continue to deleverage.
Valuation and view  IRB reported a steady performance, supported by rising toll collections.
